title: dynamic saturation guard and late-eviction prober for continuous-batcher
author: Sana Patel
release_notes: Improves continuous-batcher fairness and starvation resilience by adding a dynamic saturation guard, late-eviction probing, and refined timeout backoff heuristics. No API changes.
description:
Context and motivation:
As production traffic patterns evolved we observed intermittent starvation of small, low-token requests when load hit volatile peaks. Existing admission logic used a static saturation threshold and a single timeout ladder; that combination tended to either (a) overprotect high-throughput flows and increase latency for short requests or (b) underprotect and allow slot-hogging when model kernels experienced transient slowdowns.

Proposal and summary of changes:
This PR introduces two cooperating mechanisms to make continuous-batcher behavior more adaptive and less brittle:
1) Dynamic Saturation Guard: a feedback-driven saturation limit per-pool that decays and grows based on recent dequeue latency and kernel execution variance. It replaces the single static saturation threshold and introduces a soft-credit decay so short requests regain admission priority after a short quiet window.
2) Late-Eviction Prober: a lightweight probe thread that detects stuck KV/cache-pin or kernel stalls by performing a low-overhead "probe" admission that simulates admission without consuming warm slots; probes trigger targeted late-eviction of long-waited slots (preferred to global evictions) and mark affected kernels with a short penalty to discourage new coalesces until stabilization.
3) Adaptive timeout backoff with jitter persistence: individual requests now carry a small backoff counter that increments on soft-timeouts; the scheduler uses this to jitter retry windows to avoid synchronized replays and to prefer lower-backoff requests for head-of-queue.
4) KV pin hints integration: admission and prober now consult KV pin hint scores to avoid evicting recently pinned state; pins receive a decaying grace window.
5) Observability and safety: new metrics (saturation_guard_level, probe_evictions, probe_latency_ms, soft_timeouts) and a dashboard doc added. Extensive unit and e2e tests included.

Checklist (author):
- [x] Design doc reviewed by scheduling owners (ENG-1489)
- [x] Unit tests for saturation guard and probe behavior
- [x] E2E scenario reproducing previous starvation pattern
- [x] CI green and perf benchmark showing <=1% tail regression for p95 on stable traffic
- [x] Added observability entries and dashboard guide

Commits (high-level):
- feat(batcher): add saturation_guard type with feedback controller (Sana Patel)
- feat(batcher): implement late-eviction prober and probe admission path
- perf(scheduler): integrate request backoff counter into admission logic
- feat(kv): add pin_hints API and decaying grace window
- test: add saturation and probe unit tests + e2e replay scenario
- docs: batcher metrics and dashboard instructions

Files changed (high level):
- pkg/runtime/batcher/continuous/batcher.go: refactor admission pipeline to consult saturation guard and backoff counters (core admission logic ~120 lines changed, mostly composition).
- pkg/runtime/batcher/saturation_guard.go: new file implementing an exponential moving average controller plus soft-credit bucket and decay loop.
- pkg/runtime/batcher/eviction_probe.go: new file for probe scheduler, probe admission path, and eviction logic targeting long-waited slots.
- pkg/runtime/scheduler/queue_metrics.go: new metrics exported + labels for pool/priority.
- pkg/runtime/kv/pin_hints.go: small API to record and query recent KV pin scores; respected by eviction logic.
- internal/tests/batcher/saturation_tests.go: deterministic tests that simulate kernel stalls and verify small-request preservation.
- docs/observability/batcher-metrics.md: doc for new metrics and dashboard recipe.

Behavioral notes and trade-offs:
- The saturation guard is intentionally conservative by default; operators can tune aggressiveness via config flags but the default uses the learned controller with safe upper/lower bounds to avoid oscillation.
- Late-eviction probers target specific slots instead of mass-evictions; they may evict pinned slots only after the pin grace lapses. This lowers collateral damage but means pathological cases with long-running pinned ops still require manual inspection.
- There is a small CPU cost for the prober and the guard's background tasks; in benchmarks we saw ~0.2% CPU on a 16-core worker at 80% load. The latency benefit on small requests p50/p95 was substantial in stressed scenarios.

Testing and benchmarks:
- Unit tests included cover controller stability and correctness under synthetic jitter and kernel slowdown.
- E2E replay: previous-starvation trace replayed across a 6-hour window; p95 for <64-token requests improved from 620ms to 240ms under the same throughput.
- Regression testing: ran existing perf-canary harness; no regressions observed in model throughput or large-batch efficiency.

Review conversation (summary):
- Marcus Li: requested clearer invariants for guard growth/decay and a safety clamp to prevent runaway growth — addressed by adding min/max caps and a short-term cooldown when the controller observes 3 consecutive probe-evictions.
- Aisha Gomez: asked for stronger observability around probe-triggered evictions, and whether evictions could be correlated to kernel faults — added probe_eviction_reason tag and a small audit log line to surface in tracing.
- Evan Park: raised concern about interaction with Dedicated autoscaler; added a feature-flag to opt out of late-eviction probing for dedicated fleets pending capacity policy review.
- Follow-ups: added e2e scenario and extra unit tests; Marcus approved after these changes, Aisha approved after metrics added.

CI and rollout notes:
- CI: unit + integration + perf tests passed on first run; one flake in unrelated docs test re-run and passed.
- Rollout: feature-flag gated rollout with a gradual ramp (10% -> 50% -> 100%) over 48 hours recommended. Observability playbook added to docs/observability for on-call.

Merge outcome:
- Squash-merged into main on 2026-02-23 (merge commit a3c9f2b7d6e4b1f9c0e8d4aa).
- Post-merge: enabled on canary pool for 24 hours and then promoted per rollout notes.

Notes for SRE and platform teams:
- If you see increased probe_evictions > 5% of admissions, consider temporarily toggling probe.feature_flag=false and open an incident to inspect kernel-side stalls.
- Default saturation_guard caps are conservative; for latency-sensitive customers we recommend leaving default enabled.

If issues are found in rollout we can quickly disable both saturation guard and prober independently via runtime flags; configuration docs included in the repo.

notes_for_oncall: Watch metrics: batcher.saturation_guard_level, batcher.probe_evictions, batcher.soft_timeouts, batcher.probe_latency_ms. If probe_evictions spike, flip probe.feature_flag=false and open ENG-1510.
backport_suggestion: Candidate for backport to release/2026-02 for clusters frequently hitting starvation; manual QA recommended before backport.
testing_summary: Unit tests (saturation controller, probe path) + e2e replay: p95 reduced for small requests; CI perf harness shows no material regressions.
qa_steps: 1) Deploy to canary pool with feature-flag true. 2) Run starvation replay workload from internal/fixtures. 3) Observe metrics and traces for probe_evictions and kernel stalls. 4) If regressions, disable feature-flag and gather traces.
notes: Design rationale available in ENG-1489 thread and the PR description. The change is focused on scheduler heuristics; no API break.
human_readable_summary: Adaptive batcher improvements that prevent small-request starvation by using a feedback-driven saturation guard and a conservative probe-based late-eviction mechanism; merged to main and ramped via feature-flag.
